question: Jaipal Singh Munda is associated with which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hockey.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jaipal Singh Munda (1903-1970) was a tribal leader from Chota Nagpur (present-day Jharkhand) who captained the Indian hockey team that won the gold medal at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics, India's first Olympic hockey gold. (जयपाल सिंह मुंडा — हॉकी)

 

• He was a Munda tribal leader, educated at Oxford University (St John's College), and was among the first Indians to be selected for the Oxford Blues in hockey.

 

• After his hockey career, he became a prominent tribal rights activist and politician, founding the Adivasi Mahasabha and later serving as a member of the Constituent Assembly of India, where he strongly advocated for tribal welfare and the creation of a separate state (Jharkhand).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's hockey dominance in the early-to-mid 20th century included eight Olympic gold medals, with the first coming in 1928 (Amsterdam) under Jaipal Singh Munda's captaincy.

 

• Jaipal Singh Munda is often called "Marang Gomke" (the great leader) by the tribal community.

 

NOTE

 

• Badminton (Option 1): Not associated with Jaipal Singh Munda; notable Indian badminton players include Prakash Padukone and Saina Nehwal.

 

• Cricket (Option 2): Not his sport; he is exclusively known for hockey.

 

• Kabaddi (Option 3): Not associated with Jaipal Singh Munda.

question: Who has written the book Sangeet Bal Prakash?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vishnu Digambar Paluskar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sangeet Bal Prakash was written by Vishnu Digambar Paluskar (1872-1931), a pioneering Hindustani classical musician and music educationist. (संगीत बाल प्रकाश — विष्णु दिगंबर पलुस्कर)

 

• He founded the Gandharva Mahavidyalaya in Lahore in 1901, one of the earliest institutions in India for formal, systematic teaching of Hindustani classical music.

 

• He is credited with popularising and democratising Hindustani classical music, taking it out of exclusive royal courts and making it accessible to the general public through public concerts and standardised notation-based teaching.

 

• He belonged to the Gwalior gharana tradition and trained under Balkrishnabuwa Ichalkaranjikar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Paluskar also composed the patriotic song later associated with the freedom movement and worked to introduce music into the school curriculum via simplified textbooks like Sangeet Bal Prakash.

 

• His student Vinayakrao Patwardhan and contemporary Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande together are regarded as the two great systematisers of modern Hindustani classical music.

 

NOTE

 

• Pandit Narayan Rao (Option 1): Not associated with this book.

 

• Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande (Option 3): A contemporary musicologist known for compiling the Hindustani Sangeet Paddhati, a systematic classification of ragas — not the author of Sangeet Bal Prakash.

 

• Bhimsen Joshi (Option 4): A renowned 20th-century Hindustani classical vocalist of the Kirana gharana; not the author of this book.

question: Which of the following rivers originates from the Himalayas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ganga.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ganga originates from the Gangotri Glacier (Gaumukh) in the Himalayas, in Uttarakhand, as the Bhagirathi, which joins the Alaknanda at Devprayag to form the Ganga. (गंगा नदी — हिमालय से उत्पत्ति)

 

• It is a Himalayan (perennial, snow-and-glacier-fed) river, unlike the Peninsular rivers, and flows through Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal before draining into the Bay of Bengal.

 

• Himalayan rivers are characterised by perennial flow (fed by melting snow and glaciers even in the dry season) and youthful, actively eroding courses in their upper reaches.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major Himalayan rivers include the Indus, Brahmaputra, Yamuna and their tributaries.

 

• Peninsular rivers like the Godavari, Narmada and Tapi are rain-fed and originate from the Western Ghats or central Indian plateaus, not the Himalayas.

 

NOTE

 

• Godavari (Option 1): Originates near Trimbakeshwar in the Western Ghats, Nashik district, Maharashtra — a Peninsular river.

 

• Tapi (Option 2): Originates from the Satpura Range near Multai, Madhya Pradesh — a Peninsular river flowing westward into the Arabian Sea.

 

• Narmada (Option 3): Originates from the Amarkantak Plateau, Madhya Pradesh — a Peninsular river flowing through a rift valley into the Arabian Sea.

question: Who is the author of the book 'From Plassey to Partition and After : A History of Modern India'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sekhar Bandyopadhyay.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'From Plassey to Partition and After: A History of Modern India' is written by historian Sekhar Bandyopadhyay. (आधुनिक भारत का इतिहास — शेखर बंद्योपाध्याय)

 

• The book covers the history of modern India from the Battle of Plassey (1757) through colonial rule, nationalism and Partition (1947) and beyond, and is widely used as a standard textbook in Indian history courses.

 

• Sekhar Bandyopadhyay is a historian specialising in modern Indian history, particularly the social and political history of colonial Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Romila Thapar is a renowned historian of ancient India, known for works like 'A History of India, Vol. 1' and 'Early India'.

 

• Sumit Sarkar is a noted modern Indian historian, author of 'Modern India 1885-1947', a widely used text distinct from Bandyopadhyay's book.

 

NOTE

 

• Romila Thapar (Option 1): Specialises in ancient Indian history, not the author of this particular book.

 

• Devid Hardiman (Option 2): A historian of colonial India and subaltern studies, but not the author of this book.

 

• Sumit Sarkar (Option 4): Author of the well-known 'Modern India 1885-1947', a different (though similarly themed) textbook.

question: If a 12-year-old is found to be working in a factory manufacturing carpets, which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India will be violated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 24.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 24 of the Indian Constitution prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in any factory, mine, or other hazardous employment. (अनुच्छेद 24 — बाल श्रम निषेध)

 

• It is a Fundamental Right under the category of Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24).

 

• A 12-year-old working in a carpet-manufacturing factory falls squarely within this prohibition, since carpet-weaving is both a factory-based and hazardous occupation historically associated with child labour in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 (amended 2016) gives statutory effect to Article 24, banning employment of children below 14 in hazardous occupations and regulating conditions for adolescents (14-18).

 

• Article 24 was also strengthened by the Right to Education (Article 21A), ensuring free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14, which reinforces the prohibition on child labour.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 25 (Option 2): Guarantees freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion — unrelated to child labour.

 

• Article 23 (Option 3): Prohibits traffic in human beings, begar (forced labour) and other similar forms of forced labour — related but distinct from the specific child-in-factory prohibition, which is Article 24.

 

• Article 26 (Option 4): Deals with the freedom to manage religious affairs — unrelated to child labour.

question: Bihu festival is the main festival of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bihu is the principal harvest and cultural festival of Assam, celebrated three times a year. (बिहू पर्व — असम)

 

• The three Bihus are Rongali/Bohag Bihu (April, marks the Assamese New Year and spring), Kati/Kongali Bihu (October, associated with austerity during the growing season) and Magh/Bhogali Bihu (January, celebrates harvest and involves community feasts).

 

• Bihu is marked by traditional Bihu dance and songs, performed to the beats of the dhol, pepa (buffalo-horn pipe) and taal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rongali Bihu is the most widely celebrated of the three and is also recognised as Assam's New Year festival.

 

• Assam's other notable festivals include Ambubachi Mela at Kamakhya Temple.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option 1): Main festivals are Onam and Vishu, not Bihu.

 

• Punjab (Option 2): Main festival is Baisakhi, not Bihu.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 3): Main festivals include Teej, Gangaur and desert festivals, not Bihu.

question: Which of the following playback singers is the recipient of the Karnataka Ratna Award 2005?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhimsen Joshi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bhimsen Joshi (1922-2011), the celebrated Hindustani classical vocalist of the Kirana gharana, was conferred the Karnataka Ratna Award in 2005, the highest civilian honour of the state of Karnataka. (कर्नाटक रत्न पुरस्कार 2005 — भीमसेन जोशी)

 

• He was born in Gadag, Karnataka, and rose to become one of India's most revered Khayal vocalists, celebrated for his renditions of bhajans and classical ragas alike.

 

• He is also a recipient of the Bharat Ratna (2008), India's highest civilian award, along with the Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Karnataka Ratna award has been conferred since 1992 to individuals for outstanding contribution in fields like art, literature, science, and public service.

 

• Bhimsen Joshi co-founded the Sawai Gandharva Bhimsen Mahotsav, a major annual Hindustani classical music festival held in Pune.

 

NOTE

 

• Sistla Janaki (Option 1): A renowned South Indian playback singer, but not the Karnataka Ratna 2005 recipient.

 

• Ravindra Jain (Option 2): A noted Hindi film music director and singer, unrelated to this award.

 

• Pandit Jasraj (Option 3): A celebrated Hindustani classical vocalist of the Mewati gharana, but not the recipient of this specific award.

question: As per article 158, the Governor shall NOT be a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State specified in ________ Schedule.
solution_text:
The correct answer is First.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 158 of the Constitution lays down the conditions of the Governor's office, and clause (2) states the Governor shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or a House of the Legislature of any State specified in the First Schedule. (अनुच्छेद 158 — प्रथम अनुसूची)

 

• The First Schedule of the Constitution lists the names of the States and Union Territories and their territorial extent.

 

• Article 158 also mandates that the Governor shall not hold any other office of profit, is entitled to use official residences without payment of rent, and their emoluments/allowances cannot be diminished during their term of office.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• If a sitting member of a legislature is appointed Governor, that person is deemed to have vacated their legislative seat on the date of assuming office as Governor, as per Article 158(3).

 

• The Governor is appointed by the President under Article 155 and holds office during the pleasure of the President under Article 156.

 

NOTE

 

• Seventh Schedule (Option 1): Deals with the division of powers between the Union and States (Union, State and Concurrent Lists) — unrelated to Article 158.

 

• Fifth Schedule (Option 2): Deals with the administration of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes — unrelated to Article 158.

 

• Third Schedule (Option 4): Contains the forms of oaths and affirmations — unrelated to Article 158.

question: What is the name of the inflammatory condition that causes cracks, crusting and scaling at the corners of the mouth due to vitamin B2 deficiency?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cheilosis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Cheilosis (also called angular cheilitis/angular stomatitis) is a condition characterised by cracking, crusting and scaling at the corners of the mouth, caused primarily by a deficiency of Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin). (राइबोफ्लेविन की कमी — चीलोसिस)

 

• Riboflavin (Vitamin B2) deficiency (ariboflavinosis) also causes glossitis (inflamed tongue), sore throat, and dermatitis of the skin in addition to cheilosis.

 

• Riboflavin is found in foods like milk, eggs, green leafy vegetables and lean meats; deficiency is treated by dietary supplementation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other B-vitamin deficiency diseases: Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) deficiency causes Beriberi; Vitamin B3 (Niacin) deficiency causes Pellagra; Vitamin B12 deficiency causes Pernicious anaemia.

 

• Vitamin B2 is also essential for energy production and maintaining healthy skin, eyes and nervous system function.

 

NOTE

 

• Psoriasis (Option 2): A chronic autoimmune skin disorder causing scaly patches; not caused by vitamin B2 deficiency.

 

• Urticaria (Option 3): Commonly known as hives, an allergic skin reaction; not linked to vitamin B2 deficiency.

 

• Atopic dermatitis (Option 4): A chronic inflammatory skin condition (eczema), typically linked to allergies/genetics; not caused by vitamin B2 deficiency.

question: According to the Tea Board of India's report (2021-22), which group of states in India is the largest tea producer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Bengal and Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Tea Board of India's report (2021-22), Assam and West Bengal together are the largest tea-producing states in India, accounting for roughly 80-83% of the country's total tea production. (चाय उत्पादन — असम और पश्चिम बंगाल)

 

• Assam alone is the single largest tea-producing state, contributing more than half of India's total output, with major growing tracts in the Brahmaputra valley and Cachar.

 

• West Bengal is the second-largest producer, with tea grown in the Dooars, Terai, and the famous Darjeeling hills (Darjeeling tea has a GI tag and is known as the "Champagne of Teas").

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• South Indian tea-producing states — Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka — together account for a much smaller share (around 15-17%) of national tea production, chiefly from the Nilgiri hills.

 

• India is the second-largest tea producer in the world after China, and tea is one of India's major export commodities.

 

NOTE

 

• Andhra Pradesh and Kerala (Option 1): Andhra Pradesh has negligible tea production; not the largest producing group.

 

• Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand (Option 2): These are minor tea-producing states (notably Kangra tea), far behind Assam-West Bengal in output.

 

• Tamil Nadu and Kerala (Option 4): Together the South Indian states contribute significantly less than Assam and West Bengal.

question: Which of the following Delhi sultans introduced two coins, namely silver tanka and copper jital?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iltutmish.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Iltutmish (r. 1211-1236), the third ruler of the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, introduced two standardised coins — the silver tanka and the copper jital. (इल्तुतमिश — चांदी का टंका और तांबे का जीतल)

 

• Iltutmish is regarded as the real founder of the Delhi Sultanate as a stable, organised state — he suppressed rival claimants, organised the Iqta system, and established the "Chahalgani" (the Forty), a group of loyal Turkish nobles.

 

• He also secured formal recognition from the Abbasid Caliph in 1229, legitimising his rule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The silver tanka weighed approximately 175 grains and became the standard silver coin of the Sultanate; the copper jital was the standard base-metal coin, both remaining in use for centuries after Iltutmish.

 

• Iltutmish's daughter, Razia Sultan, went on to become the first woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.

 

NOTE

 

• Qutbuddin Aibak (Option 1): Founder of the Slave dynasty and Delhi Sultanate; began construction of the Qutub Minar but is not credited with introducing the tanka and jital.

 

• Bahlul Lodi (Option 2): Founder of the Lodi dynasty, much later (15th century); not associated with introducing these coins.

 

• Ghiyasuddin Balban (Option 3): A later Slave dynasty ruler known for the theory of kingship (Niyabat-i-Khudai) and the "blood and iron" policy, not for introducing the tanka and jital.

question: Who founded the Theosophical Society in New York in 1875?
option_1: Naoroji Furdunji and Satyendra Nath Bose
option_2: Baba Dayal Das and Madan Lal
option_4: Madame HP Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madame HP Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Theosophical Society was founded in New York, USA, in 1875 by Madame Helena Petrovna Blavatsky and Colonel Henry Steel Olcott. (थियोसोफिकल सोसाइटी — मैडम ब्लावात्स्की और कर्नल ऑलकॉट)

 

• The Society later shifted its headquarters to Adyar, Madras (Chennai) in India in 1882, from where it promoted the study of theosophy, comparative religion, philosophy and science, and the concept of universal brotherhood.

 

• Annie Besant, who joined later and became the Society's president in 1907, played a major role in the Indian Home Rule Movement and Indian nationalist politics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Theosophical Society championed the revival of Hindu and Buddhist philosophy at a time of colonial cultural denigration, contributing to a sense of Indian cultural pride.

 

• Annie Besant also founded the Central Hindu College in Varanasi, which later became part of Banaras Hindu University.

 

NOTE

 

• Naoroji Furdunji and Satyendra Nath Bose (Option 1): Not the founders of the Theosophical Society; Naoroji Furdunji was associated with early Parsi social reform.

 

• Baba Dayal Das and Madan Lal (Option 2): Baba Dayal Das founded the Nirankari movement among Sikhs, unrelated to the Theosophical Society.

 

• Ramabai Ranade and GK Devadhar (Option 3): Associated with the Seva Sadan social reform movement in Maharashtra, not the Theosophical Society.

question: During the period of 1947 to 1990, how many five-year plans were completed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Between 1947 and 1990, India completed seven Five-Year Plans, from the First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) through the Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985-90). (सात पंचवर्षीय योजनाएं — 1951 से 1990)

 

• Planning in independent India began with the establishment of the Planning Commission in 1950, and the First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) focused on agriculture and irrigation (based on the Harrod-Domar model).

 

• There were "Plan Holidays" from 1966-69 (after the failure of the Third Plan, due to wars and drought) and 1979-80 (after the Janata government's Rolling Plan/Sixth Plan 1978-83 was discontinued), during which annual plans were used instead of a Five-Year Plan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The plans, in order till 1990: 1st (1951-56), 2nd (1956-61), 3rd (1961-66), Plan Holiday (1966-69), 4th (1969-74), 5th (1974-78), Rolling Plan (1978-80), 6th (1980-85), 7th (1985-90).

 

• The Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015, ending the era of Five-Year Plans; the last (12th) plan ran 2012-17.

 

NOTE

 

• 6 (Option 1): Undercounts the number of completed plans by 1990.

 

• 9 (Option 3): Overcounts; nine plans would extend well beyond 1990 (up to the late 1990s).

 

• 8 (Option 4): Overcounts by one; the Eighth Plan (1992-97) began after 1990, following a gap year in 1990-92.

question: Name the straight chain alkane having chemical formula C9H20, which is used as a research chemical and in making biodegradable detergents.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nonane.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nonane is the straight-chain (n-alkane) hydrocarbon with the chemical formula C9H20, consisting of nine carbon atoms in a single unbranched chain. (नोनेन — C9H20)

 

• It is used as a research/laboratory chemical, a component of kerosene and gasoline, and in the synthesis of biodegradable detergents (linear alkylbenzene-based).

 

• Alkanes are named using the prefix indicating the number of carbon atoms plus the suffix "-ane": nonane comes from the Greek/Latin prefix "non-" (nine).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The homologous series of straight-chain alkanes: Methane (C1), Ethane (C2), Propane (C3), Butane (C4), Pentane (C5), Hexane (C6), Heptane (C7), Octane (C8), Nonane (C9), Decane (C10).

 

• Straight-chain (linear) alkylbenzene sulfonates, derived from such alkanes, are widely used as biodegradable surfactants in detergents, replacing older non-biodegradable branched-chain alkylbenzene sulfonates.

 

NOTE

 

• Dodecane (Option 2): Has the formula C12H26 (12 carbons), not C9H20.

 

• Nonadecane (Option 3): Has the formula C19H40 (19 carbons), not C9H20.

 

• Icosane (Option 4): Has the formula C20H42 (20 carbons), not C9H20.

question: When you take Lead nitrate powder in a boiling tube and heat it, you will observe the emission of brown fumes that are of _____________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nitrogen dioxide.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On heating, lead nitrate [Pb(NO3)2] undergoes thermal decomposition to give lead oxide (PbO), nitrogen dioxide (NO2) and oxygen (O2) gas. (लेड नाइट्रेट का अपघटन — नाइट्रोजन डाइऑक्साइड)

 

• The characteristic reddish-brown fumes observed are due to the release of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) gas — this is a classic example of a thermal decomposition reaction.

 

• Balanced equation: 2Pb(NO3)2 → 2PbO + 4NO2↑ + O2↑.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• This reaction is often called the "crackling camphor" or decrepitation reaction in demonstrations because of the crackling sound and vivid brown fumes it produces, making it a popular classroom experiment.

 

• Nitrogen dioxide (NO2) is also a major air pollutant produced by vehicle emissions and combustion of fossil fuels.

 

NOTE

 

• Nitrous oxide (Option 1): Chemical formula N2O, a colourless gas ("laughing gas"), not the brown fume produced here.

 

• Nitric oxide (Option 2): Chemical formula NO, a colourless gas that turns brown only on contact with air (forming NO2) — it is not itself the brown fume directly emitted.

 

• Dinitrogen trioxide (Option 4): Chemical formula N2O3, a blue solid/pale blue liquid, not the reddish-brown gas released here.

question: Who among the following sent Megasthenes to the court of Chandragupta Maurya?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seleucus I Nicator.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Seleucus I Nicator, the Greek general who founded the Seleucid Empire after Alexander the Great's death, sent Megasthenes as his ambassador to the court of Chandragupta Maurya in Pataliputra. (मेगस्थनीज — सेल्यूकस निकेटर द्वारा भेजा गया राजदूत)

 

• This followed the treaty between Seleucus and Chandragupta Maurya (c. 305 BCE), in which Seleucus ceded territories (parts of present-day Afghanistan) to Chandragupta in exchange for war elephants and a marriage alliance.

 

• Megasthenes wrote "Indica", a detailed account of Mauryan society, administration, geography and culture, which survives today only in fragments quoted by later Greek and Roman writers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Later Seleucid king Antiochus III is not connected to Megasthenes; instead Deimachus, another Greek ambassador, was sent by Antiochus I Soter (Seleucus's son) to the court of Bindusara, Chandragupta's successor.

 

• The Indica of Megasthenes is a key primary source for reconstructing Mauryan administration, including its city governance and army organisation.

 

NOTE

 

• Antiochus I Soter (Option 1): Son and successor of Seleucus I; he sent Deimachus to Bindusara's court, not Megasthenes to Chandragupta.

 

• Alexander III (Option 2, Alexander the Great): Invaded north-western India (327-325 BCE) before the Mauryan period; did not send Megasthenes.

 

• Antiochus III (Option 4): A later Seleucid king ("the Great"), from a much later period, unconnected to Megasthenes' mission.

question: Which of the following states is one of those states that have no Panchayati Raj Institution at all?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagaland.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nagaland is one of the Indian states where the 73rd Constitutional Amendment (Panchayati Raj provisions) does not apply, and it has no Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs). (पंचायती राज संस्था नहीं — नागालैंड)

 

• Under Article 243-M, the Panchayati Raj provisions do not extend to Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram, where traditional tribal self-governance systems (based on customary tribal councils) continue instead.

 

• In Nagaland, local governance is instead handled through traditional Village Councils and Village Development Boards, rooted in customary Naga tribal practices, protected under Article 371A of the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Besides Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram, Panchayati Raj provisions also do not apply to certain Scheduled and Tribal Areas and to hill areas of Manipur under district councils, and to Union Territories of Delhi, unless extended by Parliament.

 

• The 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions as the third tier of rural governance across most of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Assam (Option 1): Has functioning Panchayati Raj Institutions under the 73rd Amendment.

 

• Gujarat (Option 2): Has functioning Panchayati Raj Institutions and was among the early adopters of the three-tier Panchayati Raj system.

 

• Punjab (Option 4): Has functioning Panchayati Raj Institutions under the 73rd Amendment.

question: In Pradhan Mantri Gramin Awaas Yojana, the cost of unit assistance is shared between Central and State Governments in the ratio ___________ for the North-Eastern and the Himalayan states.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 90 : 10.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G), the cost of unit assistance is shared between the Centre and States in the ratio of 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States, recognising their special category status and resource constraints. (प्रधानमंत्री ग्रामीण आवास योजना — 90:10 अनुपात, पूर्वोत्तर व हिमालयी राज्य)

 

• For the rest of India, the standard sharing ratio is 60:40 between the Centre and States.

 

• For Union Territories, the Centre bears 100% of the cost.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• PMAY-G aims to provide a pucca house with basic amenities to all houseless households and those living in kutcha/dilapidated houses in rural India, originally targeted for completion by 2022 ("Housing for All").

 

• The scheme provides financial assistance of Rs. 1.20 lakh in plain areas and Rs. 1.30 lakh in hilly/difficult areas/IAP districts (as originally structured; amounts have since been revised upward).

 

NOTE

 

• 60:40 (Option 2): This is the Centre-State sharing ratio for the general/plain areas of India, not for NE and Himalayan states.

 

• 45:55 (Option 3): Not a ratio used under PMAY-G.

 

• 50:50 (Option 4): Not the ratio applicable to NE and Himalayan states under this scheme.

question: Which of the following is an example of capital receipts?
option_1: Revenue from the sale of government assets
solution_text:
The correct answer is Revenue from the sale of government assets.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Capital receipts are government receipts that either create a liability or reduce (financial) assets — such as borrowings, recovery of loans, and proceeds from disinvestment/sale of government assets. (पूंजीगत प्राप्तियां — सरकारी संपत्ति की बिक्री से आय)

 

• When the government sells an asset (e.g., disinvestment of a PSU, sale of land/buildings), it reduces the government's asset base, which is the defining characteristic of a capital receipt.

 

• This is distinct from revenue receipts, which are recurring receipts that neither create a liability nor reduce an asset (e.g., tax revenue, interest earned, fees).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other examples of capital receipts include market borrowings, loans from foreign governments/institutions, and recovery of loans given by the government.

 

• The Union Budget of India classifies total receipts into Revenue Receipts and Capital Receipts, as per Article 112 of the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Taxes on income (Option 2): A revenue receipt — it is a recurring, regular source of government income that doesn't affect assets/liabilities in the capital sense.

 

• Interest on government bonds (Option 3): Wording here refers to interest income earned by the government, which is a revenue receipt.

 

• Grants-in-aid from other governments (Option 4): Classified as a revenue receipt, since it does not create any liability or reduce government assets.

question: 'Drain of Wealth', a critique of the colonial exploitation, was given by which of the following nationalist leaders?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dadabhai Naoroji.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The "Drain of Wealth" theory, which argued that Britain was systematically draining India's wealth and resources without adequate compensation, was propounded by Dadabhai Naoroji. (धन-अपवाह सिद्धांत — दादाभाई नौरोजी)

 

• He elaborated this theory in his influential book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India" (1901), using early national income estimates to demonstrate the economic exploitation of India under colonial rule.

 

• Naoroji, known as the "Grand Old Man of India," was a founding member of the Indian National Congress and the first Indian to become a Member of the British House of Commons.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other early nationalist economic critics ('Economic Nationalists') included R.C. Dutt (author of "The Economic History of India") and M.G. Ranade, who also highlighted colonial economic exploitation.

 

• Naoroji's Drain Theory became a foundational critique used by the moderates in the early nationalist movement to demand economic and political reforms.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajendra Prasad (Option 2): First President of independent India; not associated with the Drain of Wealth theory.

 

• Chakravarti Rajagopalachari (Option 3): Freedom fighter and first Indian Governor-General of independent India; not associated with this theory.

 

• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel (Option 4): Known as the "Iron Man of India" for the integration of princely states; not associated with the Drain of Wealth theory.

question: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Aves (birds) class?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pteropus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pteropus is a genus of fruit bats (flying foxes), which belong to the class Mammalia, not Aves — bats are mammals capable of flight, distinguished from birds by features like fur, mammary glands, and a wing structure of skin stretched over elongated finger bones. (चमगादड़ — स्तनधारी वर्ग, पक्षी वर्ग नहीं)

 

• Psittacula is a genus of parakeets (true parrots), belonging to class Aves.

 

• Neophron is the genus of the Egyptian vulture, a bird of prey, belonging to class Aves.

 

• Struthio is the genus of the ostrich, the largest living bird, belonging to class Aves.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bats (order Chiroptera, which includes Pteropus) are the only mammals capable of true, sustained flight.

 

• Class Aves is characterised by feathers, beaks without teeth, laying hard-shelled eggs, and a lightweight but strong skeleton.

 

NOTE

 

• Psittacula (Option 1): A genus of parrots/parakeets — a true bird (Aves), incorrect as the answer to "NOT a member of Aves".

 

• Neophron (Option 2): Genus of the Egyptian vulture — a true bird (Aves), incorrect as the answer.

 

• Struthio (Option 4): Genus of the ostrich — a true bird (Aves), incorrect as the answer.

question: In January 2023, Koneru Humpy won India's first-ever silver medal at the __________ held in Almaty, Kazakhstan.
solution_text:
The correct answer is World Blitz Chess Championship.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Koneru Humpy won India's first-ever silver medal in the women's section of the FIDE World Blitz Chess Championship 2022, held in Almaty, Kazakhstan (results concluded around late December 2022/early January 2023). (कोनेरू हम्पी — विश्व ब्लिट्ज़ शतरंज चैंपियनशिप, रजत पदक)

 

• The event was part of the combined FIDE World Rapid and Blitz Chess Championships 2022, where Koneru Humpy competed in both formats, achieving her best individual result in the Blitz section.

 

• Koneru Humpy is one of India's most accomplished woman Grandmasters, a former Women's World Rapid Chess Champion (2019) and a multiple-time Indian and Asian champion.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Koneru Humpy became the second woman in history (after Judit Polgár) to cross a FIDE rating of 2600.

 

• She hails from Andhra Pradesh and has been a leading figure in Indian women's chess for over two decades, alongside players like R. Vaishali and D. Harika.

 

NOTE

 

• FIDE World Chess Championship (Option 1): The classical world championship title (contested by open-category top players like Ding Liren, Gukesh D); Koneru Humpy's Almaty 2022-23 medal was not in this event.

 

• World Correspondence Chess Championship (Option 3): A distinct, much slower postal/online chess format unrelated to this event.

 

• World Rapid Chess Championship (Option 4): Held alongside the Blitz event at the same venue, but Koneru Humpy's historic silver at this particular time was specifically in the Blitz format.

question: In which month is the Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) located around 20°N-25°N latitude (over the Gangetic plain)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is July.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) shifts northward during the Northern Hemisphere summer, and by July, it is positioned around 20°N-25°N latitude, roughly over the Gangetic plain, marking the peak/mature phase of the Indian Southwest Monsoon. (अंतःउष्णकटिबंधीय अभिसरण क्षेत्र — जुलाई माह, गंगा के मैदान)

 

• The ITCZ is a low-pressure belt near the equator where the north-east and south-east trade winds converge; its seasonal north-south migration (following the apparent movement of the sun) drives the monsoon system over the Indian subcontinent.

 

• Over the Indian region, this northward-shifted summer ITCZ (sometimes called the "monsoon trough") runs from the Thar Desert through the Gangetic plains to the Bay of Bengal, and its position strongly influences monsoon rainfall distribution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• During winter (northeast monsoon season), the ITCZ shifts south of the equator, contributing to the retreat of the southwest monsoon and dry conditions over most of India.

 

• The seasonal shifting of the ITCZ is one of the several theories (along with jet streams and differential heating of land-sea) explaining the onset and progress of the Indian monsoon.

 

NOTE

 

• May (Option 1): ITCZ is still positioned closer to the equator/southern latitudes just before monsoon onset, not yet at 20°N-25°N.

 

• August (Option 2): By August, the ITCZ has already been established over the Gangetic plain for some time (since around July) and the specific northward positioning described is characteristic of July.

 

• June (Option 3): Marks the onset of the monsoon over India (Kerala coast), but the ITCZ typically reaches around 20°N-25°N (Gangetic plain) as the monsoon becomes well established, in July.

question: Mirabai Chanu secured a silver medal at which Commonwealth Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2014.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saikhom Mirabai Chanu made her Commonwealth Games debut in 2014 (Glasgow), winning a silver medal in the women's 48 kg weightlifting category. (मीराबाई चानू — 2014 राष्ट्रमंडल खेल, रजत पदक)

 

• She went on to win gold at the 2018 Gold Coast Commonwealth Games (48 kg) and gold at the 2022 Birmingham Commonwealth Games (49 kg), later completing a hat-trick of golds at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games.

 

• Mirabai Chanu is a two-time Olympic medallist — silver at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics (49 kg) and bronze at the Paris 2024 Olympics (49 kg) — the first Indian woman to win an Olympic weightlifting medal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mirabai Chanu hails from Nongpok Kakching, Manipur, and is a recipient of the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna and Padma Shri.

 

• She also won a silver medal at the 2017 World Weightlifting Championships, becoming the first Indian in over two decades to win a Weightlifting World Championship medal.

 

NOTE

 

• 2010 (Option 1): Mirabai Chanu did not compete in the 2010 Delhi Commonwealth Games.

 

• 2022 (Option 3): She won a gold medal (not silver) at the 2022 Birmingham Commonwealth Games.

 

• 2018 (Option 4): She won a gold medal (not silver) at the 2018 Gold Coast Commonwealth Games.

question: The New Moore Island is in geographic proximity to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bangladesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• New Moore Island (also called South Talpatti Island in Bangladesh) was a small, uninhabited offshore sandbar/island located in the Bay of Bengal, near the mouth of the Hariabhanga River, in close geographic proximity to Bangladesh (and India's West Bengal coast). (न्यू मूर द्वीप — बांग्लादेश के निकट)

 

• The island was the subject of a long-standing territorial dispute between India and Bangladesh, as it emerged after a 1970 cyclone near the maritime boundary between the two countries.

 

• The island submerged/disappeared due to rising sea levels around 2010, effectively ending the dispute, though it remained relevant to the subsequent India-Bangladesh maritime boundary arbitration (2014), which was resolved by the Permanent Court of Arbitration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The island was known by different names: New Moore Island (India), South Talpatti Island (Bangladesh).

 

• The 2014 Permanent Court of Arbitration verdict on the India-Bangladesh maritime boundary awarded a significant portion of the disputed Bay of Bengal waters to Bangladesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Pakistan (Option 1): Not geographically close to New Moore Island, which lies in the eastern Bay of Bengal.

 

• Myanmar (Option 2): Not the country in immediate proximity to New Moore Island; the island was near the India-Bangladesh boundary, not the India-Myanmar boundary.

 

• Sri Lanka (Option 4): Located in the southern part of the Indian peninsula, far from New Moore Island's location in the northern Bay of Bengal.
